channel.title: BusinessHub.cy — Compliance
channel.description: Latest Compliance stories from BusinessHub.cy, Cyprus Edition.

item.title: Sustainability: Council and Parliament strike deal on simpler transparency rules for financial product
item.description: The EU has agreed on a revised SFDR framework, introducing three new product categories to simplify sustainability reporting and combat greenwashing.

item.title: Every child has the right to grow up in safety and to dream about their future, says Special Envoy on children of Ukraine
item.description: The Council of Europe's Special Envoy highlights the ongoing violations of Ukrainian children's rights, emphasizing international cooperation for protection, return, and reintegration amid the ongoing conflict.

item.title: Delivering a more consistent and risk-based approach to AML/CFT across Europe: Rikke-Louise Ørum Petersen speaks at AMLP Forum
item.description: AMLA Executive Rikke-Louise Ørum Petersen outlined the transition toward a unified European AML/CFT framework, emphasizing the Single Rulebook and upcoming direct supervision starting in 2028.

item.title: Statement by President von der Leyen on the signature of the EU-Indonesia Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement and the Investment Protection Agreement
item.description: The EU and Indonesia have signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), removing trade duties and establishing a stable legal framework for investment between the two regions.

item.title: The CBC hosted a successful coin design workshop
item.description: The Central Bank of Cyprus hosted a professional workshop to train Cypriot artists in coin design, aiming to localize and diversify future numismatic production.

item.title: Foreign Direct Investment 2025
item.description: The Central Bank of Cyprus reports a 4.1% rise in inward FDI to €381.4 billion for 2025, with notable growth in Asian partnerships and non-SPE domestic investments.

item.title: Commission partially greenlights Poland's final payment request for €12.7 billion under NextGenerationEU
item.description: The European Commission partially approved Poland's €12.7 billion recovery fund payment, highlighting successful reforms in cybersecurity, e-health, and energy infrastructure despite a minor delay in port upgrades.

item.title: Commission greenlights Ireland's final payment request for €225 million under NextGenerationEU
item.description: The European Commission approved Ireland's final €225 million RRF payment request, notably highlighting the strengthening of anti-money laundering frameworks through new administrative financial sanction regimes.

item.title: Commission greenlights Portugal's final payment request for €4.7 billion under NextGenerationEU
item.description: The European Commission approved Portugal's final €4.7 billion RRF payment, signaling successful completion of national reforms in tax simplification, healthcare, and green energy.

item.title: Commission partially greenlights Malta's final payment request for €61.7 million under NextGenerationEU
item.description: The European Commission partially approved Malta's €61.7 million payment request under the Recovery and Resilience Facility, withholding funds due to an unfulfilled reform regarding judicial independence.

item.title: The EBA publishes updated information on third-country groups and branches operating in the EU/EEA
item.description: The EBA's 2026 update details 441 third-country banking groups in the EU, highlighting strict compliance with Intermediate EU Parent Undertaking (IPU) requirements and branch oversight.

item.title: Albania: Staff Concluding Statement of the 2026 Article IV Mission
item.description: IMF's 2026 Article IV mission reports strong growth for Albania, urging continued structural reforms and fiscal vigilance as the country progresses toward EU accession.

item.title: Commission disburses €7.9 billion to strengthen Ukraine's financial stability and advance reform efforts
item.description: The EU has disbursed €7.9 billion to Ukraine, the largest payment under the Ukraine Facility, following progress in judicial, anti-corruption, and financial market reforms.

item.title: Commission partially greenlights Bulgaria's final payment request for €1.82 billion under NextGenerationEU
item.description: The European Commission partially approved Bulgaria's €1.82 billion payment request under NextGenerationEU, highlighting progress in energy, anti-corruption, and transport while noting six unfulfilled milestones.

item.title: Commission partially greenlights Belgium's final payment request for €1.38 billion under NextGenerationEU
item.description: The European Commission partially approved Belgium's €1.38 billion final RRF payment, signaling stricter enforcement of milestone fulfillment for EU-funded recovery projects.

item.title: Commission greenlights Greece's final payment requests for €11.32 billion under NextGenerationEU
item.description: The European Commission has approved Greece's final RRF payment requests totaling €11.32 billion, confirming the completion of 172 milestones across energy, digital, and administrative sectors.

item.title: Commission greenlights Slovenia's seventh and final payment request for €271.8 million under NextGenerationEU
item.description: The European Commission approved Slovenia's final RRF payment request of €271.8 million following the successful completion of 60 milestones and targets.

item.title: Daily news - 19 Nov 2026
item.description: The European Commission has approved over €16 billion in RRF payments to five member states and disbursed €7.9 billion to Ukraine to support stability and reforms.

item.title: Fraudulent use of the Egmont Group’s name
item.description: The Egmont Group warns of scammers impersonating the organization to solicit fees or verify transactions, targeting the public and financial sectors.

item.title: Connecting the pieces in the fight against financial crime
item.description: The Egmont Group emphasizes the necessity of multi-sectoral cooperation and unified intelligence sharing to combat financial crime within the virtual asset ecosystem.

item.title: The EBA reports growing market share of third-country bank subsidiaries in the EU and reduced foreign currency mismatches
item.description: The EBA reports a rise in third-country bank market share to 10.22% and a significant reduction in US dollar currency mismatches across EU banking institutions.

item.title: EU/EEA banks continue to display resilience amid sovereign debt pressures, borrower vulnerabilities and rising cyber threats
item.description: EU/EEA banks show resilience and growth through mid-2026, though rising cyber threats, AI adoption risks, and SME vulnerabilities require heightened compliance vigilance.

item.title: EU and Jordan advance strategic partnership backed by €3 billion to boost investment, create jobs and strengthen regional stability
item.description: The EU and Jordan signed a €3 billion strategic partnership and a €500 million assistance agreement to boost economic modernization, energy, and digital investment through 2027.

item.title: Speech by President von der Leyen at the EU-Jordan Investment Conference
item.description: The EU is deepening economic ties with Jordan through strategic investments in transport, energy, and digital infrastructure to enhance regional stability and secure trade routes.

item.title: Statement by Executive Vice-President Mînzatu and Commissioner Lahbib ahead of European Equal Pay Day
item.description: The EU marks Equal Pay Day, emphasizing the June 2026 deadline for Cyprus and other member states to transpose the Pay Transparency Directive into national law.

item.title: Commission decides to refer Austria to the Court of Justice of the European Union for incorrectly applying the European arrest warrant
item.description: The European Commission is suing Austria for improperly refusing European Arrest Warrants involving its own nationals, violating the principle of mutual recognition in EU criminal law.

item.title: Commission decides to refer Poland to the Court of Justice of the European Union for failing to align its rules with the Seveso III Directive
item.description: The European Commission is referring Poland to the CJEU for failing to correctly transpose the Seveso III Directive regarding industrial accident prevention and safety transparency.

item.title: Commission greenlights the Netherlands' fifth and final payment request for €1.7 billion under NextGenerationEU
item.description: The EU Commission approved the Netherlands' final €1.7 billion RRF payment, marking the complete implementation of their national recovery plan ahead of the 2026 facility closure.

item.title: Statement on the incident at today's Cancer Summit
item.description: The European Commission addressed a security or procedural incident at the European Cancer Summit, highlighting the sensitivity of high-level health policy gatherings.

item.title: Almost €24 billion mobilised and 614 projects awarded for their support to critical technologies in Europe, according to Commission report
item.description: The EU's STEP initiative has mobilized €24 billion and awarded 614 project seals to accelerate critical technologies, now including a significant expansion into defense and dual-use sectors.

item.title: November infringements package: key decisions
item.description: The European Commission has launched infringement procedures against Greece, Malta, and others for failing to designate competent authorities for the EU Deforestation Regulation enforcement.

item.title: Daily news - 18 Nov 2026
item.description: The EU's STEP initiative has mobilized €23.9 billion for critical technologies, now expanding to include defense and dual-use innovations to bolster European competitiveness and security.

item.title: TC 9/2026 – Statement by the statutory auditor regarding Public Country-by-Country Reporting (PCbCR)
item.description: Auditors must now confirm if large multinational groups have fulfilled their new Public Country-by-Country Reporting obligations in Cyprus.

item.title: Official Launch of the ICPAC-ICAEW Co-Branded IFRS and ISA Certificates
item.description: ICPAC and ICAEW launch discounted, co-branded IFRS and ISA certificates to enhance the technical proficiency of accounting and audit professionals in Cyprus.

item.title: Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP): October 2026
item.description: Cyprus's HICP rose 5.4% in October 2026, driven by a 24.1% surge in energy costs and significant increases in transport and housing expenses.

item.title: New tailored assessment process and other measures to support low-capacity countries
item.description: The FATF introduces a tailored assessment process for low-capacity countries to prioritize high-impact AML/CFT reforms over exhaustive legal frameworks.

item.title: DRSP supervisory responsibilities remain unchanged following ESMA assessment
item.description: ESMA maintains direct supervision of major Data Reporting Services Providers (DRSPs) for 2025, while smaller entities remain under national oversight by CySEC.

item.title: Press Release – Stereotypes and inequalities hinder women's financial independence
item.description: CyFLEC workshops reveal a significant gender gap in financial literacy in Cyprus, calling for institutional action to empower women's financial independence.

item.title: Dissolution and liquidation of investment compartment of CRANE FUND of RAIF C3ALLURO RAIF V.C.I.C. LTD
item.description: CySEC has announced the commencement of the dissolution and liquidation process for the CRANE FUND investment compartment of C3ALLURO RAIF V.C.I.C. Ltd.

item.title: Dissolution and liquidation of RAIF ILUVATAR CAPITAL RAIF V.C.I.C. LTD
item.description: CySEC has announced the commencement of the dissolution and liquidation process for ILUVATAR CAPITAL RAIF V.C.I.C. PLC, managed by AUDE FM Limited.

item.title: CySEC Warnings To Investors Overview
item.description: The Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC) maintains a centralized registry of warnings to alert investors about unauthorized entities and fraudulent activities.

item.title: Video message by President von der Leyen at the Reykjavik Global Forum
item.description: EU Commission President von der Leyen reaffirms commitment to gender equality, focusing on leadership, equal pay, and digital safety for women across the European Union.

item.title: EU endorses Global Electrification Pledge at COP31
item.description: The EU has endorsed the Global Electrification Pledge at COP31, targeting 46% electrification by 2040 to phase out fossil fuels and enhance energy security.

item.title: Commission proposes €45 billion in additional financial support for Ukraine in 2027
item.description: The European Commission has proposed a €45 billion financial support package for Ukraine in 2027, focusing on military aid, budget support, and defense industry integration.

item.title: Questions and answers on new financial support package for Ukraine for 2027
item.description: The EU proposes a €45 billion loan package for Ukraine for 2027 to cover critical defense and budgetary gaps, utilizing market borrowing and existing facility mechanisms.

item.title: Commission proposes to boost advanced materials for Europe's innovation and industrial leadership
item.description: The EU has launched an Advanced Materials agenda aiming for a 20% increase in investment and startups by 2035 to secure industrial leadership and economic security.

item.title: Video message by President von der Leyen at the European Cancer Summit
item.description: President von der Leyen reaffirmed the EU's €4 billion commitment to cancer care, emphasizing expanded screening, equal treatment access, and the legislative 'right to be forgotten' for survivors.

item.title: Press point by President von der Leyen together with Commissioners Dombrovskis and Kubilius on an Instrument for Coordinated Support to Ukraine
item.description: The EU proposes a €45 billion 'Instrument for Coordinated Support to Ukraine' for 2027 alongside a 22nd sanctions package against Russia.

item.title: Remarks by Commissioners Dombrovskis and Kubilius on an Instrument for Coordinated Support to Ukraine
item.description: The European Commission proposed a €45 billion support package for Ukraine for 2027, financed via EU market borrowing and repaid through future Russian sovereign asset revenues.

item.title: Commission opens Erasmus+ 2027 call with over €5.3 billion for wider opportunities in education, training, youth and sport
item.description: The European Commission launched the 2027 Erasmus+ call with €5.3 billion, prioritizing AI-ready education, vocational excellence, and basic skills development across Europe.
